n0.text:
Something is growing at {place}, in a pattern, and the pattern is a spiral that closes on a point rather than opening from one.
It is the only living thing the sweep has found here, it covers nine hectares, and {instrument} says it has doubled since the ship made orbit.

choices.text: Walk to the centre of the spiral.
Take a sample from the edge.
Burn a firebreak and watch what it does.

a.text: The growth gets {denser and quieter|thicker and quieter} towards the middle. At the centre it has grown around something that it did not grow, and has been careful about it.

choices.text: Leave it and log the position.

b.text:
{The sample fights the knife.|The sample argues with the knife.} It is not tough; it is unwilling.
In the tube it goes on moving, and by the time the team is back at the lander it has arranged itself into the same spiral, {one centimetre|a centimetre|half an inch} across.

choices.text: Put it back where it came from.

c.text:
The firebreak burns {a clean line|a clean lane} across the spiral's arm.
The growth does not try to cross it. It goes round, in both directions, and meets itself behind the away team in under {few} minutes.

choices.text: Stand and fight it back to the lander.

a1.text: It comes free in {a wet handful|a wet double handful} of stems and what is inside has been kept alive, {on purpose|deliberately}, by something with no reason to keep anything alive.

a2.text: The team backs out along its own trail. Behind them the spiral closes over the gap at walking pace, and the centre is {exactly|precisely} where it was, and {exactly|precisely} as hidden.

b1.text: Sealed, monitored, and worth {a great deal|a good deal|rather a lot} to the right laboratory. The ship's biology bay is a livelier place than it was, and {nobody|no one} sleeps quite as well.

b2.text:
It is taken back and set down at the edge, and the whole spiral shifts a metre towards the lander {and then|then|and after that} stops, which everyone agrees to record as wind.
Something is left on {ground} where the sample lay.

c1.text: {It is not a plant|Whatever it is, it is not a plant} and it does not burn a second time.

c2.text:
{Everyone gets aboard.|Everybody gets aboard.} The sample kits, the cutter and one boot do not.
{leader} is last up the ladder and does not look back, and says afterwards that it was not chasing them, it was seeing them off.

n0.text:
The transmission is a voice, in a language the ship's tables get to eighty per cent of, and it is asking for help by name. Not the ship's name. {leader}'s.
The source is a shelter at {place}, dug in against {hazard} and holding pressure.

choices.text: Cut the power to the shelter first.
Ask it how it knows the name.

a.text:
{The door cycles before anyone touches it.|The door cycles before a hand goes near it.} Inside is one room, one chair, one light, and a person in a suit {two generations|a generation|three generations} out of date sitting with their back to the door.
They do not turn around. They say they have been practising this for {a long time|a good while|longer than anybody says}.

b.text:
{The team traces the feed and pulls it.|The team follows the feed back and pulls it.} The shelter goes dark; the voice does not stop.
It has not been using the shelter's power for a {very|remarkably} long time. {It is being polite.|It has been being polite.}

choices.text: Strip the shelter for parts and leave.

c.text:
The question gets {a long pause|a very long pause}, which is the first honest thing in the exchange.
Then: it does not know the name. It knows the shape of whoever is listening, and it fits a name to it. It has been fitting names to listeners {since before this world had an atmosphere|since before there was air on this world}.

a1.text:
It takes {an hour|the better part of an hour|two hours}. They were on a survey that never filed, they have been alone since before the party was born, and they are not asking to be rescued. {They are asking to be remembered.|What they are asking for is to be remembered.}
They give {leader} everything they have left, which is not much, and it is more than the ship deserves.

a2.text: {The suit is empty|There is nobody in the suit} and has been empty for a {very|remarkably} long time, and the voice keeps talking out of the chair, out of the walls, out of the away team's own helmets.

b1.text: Inside is {lots} years of somebody's handwriting on {every flat surface|every flat surface in the place}, and at the end of it, in the last clear space by the door, an apology addressed to whoever came.

b2.text: Good hardware, well maintained, and the team is up and away in {ninety minutes|an hour and a half|two hours}. The voice is still on the band when the ship makes its burn out of orbit.

c1.text: It wants what it has always wanted, and it explains this at length, and none of it survives the trip back up as anything the crew can repeat. What survives is in {leader}'s hands, and {nobody|no one} remembers being handed it.

c2.text: {The band goes quiet.|The band goes flat and quiet.} The team walks back across {ground} in a silence that everybody is grateful for, and the shelter does not call after them, which is somehow the unkindest part.

n0.text:
The signal is a distress carrier, and it has been running long enough that {a|nobody expects an answer|the power that made it should have failed twice over}. It comes from {place}: a hull, broken across the middle, with {remnant} beside it.
{leader} takes the away team down. Up close the wreck is older than the transmission, and the transmission is older than anyone aboard.

choices.text: Follow the cable running out of the wreck.

a.text:
Inside, the crew compartment is dry and tidy and everything is stowed. {Nobody|No one} left in a hurry. There are no bodies.
A locker at the back has been sealed from the outside, and {sound} is coming from behind it.

choices.text: Take the log recorder and go.

b.text:
The cable runs out over {ground} for two kilometres and ends at a mast driven into the surface, still powered, still aimed at a point in the sky where there is nothing to aim at.
{wrongness}.

choices.text: Cut the mast down and take the core.
Point the mast at the ship and listen.

c.text:
The team works the wreck the way a wreck is meant to be worked: panels off, cells out, anything with a serial number into the bags. {It goes quickly.|It goes quickly enough.}
Halfway through, {instrument} shows {a second heat source|a second source of heat} under the hull.

choices.text: Take what is in the bags and lift.

a1.text: {The seal gives.|The seal lets go.} Whatever the crew shut in there had been waiting with the patience of a thing that does not need to breathe, and it comes out at {leader} first.

a2.text:
The recorder comes out with its casing intact. Two hundred hours of watch reports, {and then|then|and after that} one voice, on the last day, saying that the ship is not where the ship thinks it is.
{Nobody|No one} opens the locker. The team is back aboard inside the hour.

b1.text: The core comes out of the mast {in one piece|whole|in a single piece}, heavier than it has any business being, and the distress carrier stops the moment it is clear of the housing. The silence afterwards is the loudest thing on the recording.

b2.text:
Turned around, the mast plays back the last {many} seconds of everything the away team has said, in their own voices, before they have finished saying it.
{leader} calls the walk short. The team comes up shaken and one of them will not talk about it.

c1.text: Under the hull is a reactor {the size of a barrel|no bigger than a barrel}, still lit, still governed, and salvage of that quality does not come along {twice|two separate times} in a career.

c2.text: The bags come up heavy with {cells, plate and cable|cells, plate, cable}. {Nobody|No one} looks at the second heat source again, and the ship is out of the system before anybody decides they should have.

n0.text:
There is no ground to land on. The signal comes from a fixed depth in {place}, holding station in an atmosphere that should have carried anything away in an hour.
{leader} takes the capsule down. {ground} closes over the ports at nine kilometres.

choices.text: Go below it and look up.
Grapple it and haul it up.

a.text:
At depth it resolves out of the haze: a structure, not a wreck, {built to float here|built to sit here|made to float here}, with lights on in a pattern that is not for navigation.
{There is a dock.|There is a dock on it.} It is the right size.

b.text: Below it the pressure is at the capsule's rating and the view up is {worth it|worth the rating}: the thing is not floating. It is standing on a column of something that goes down past the capsule, past the sounder's range, {past any floor this world has|past any bottom this world has}.

choices.text: Take a sample of the column and go.

c.text:
The grapple takes hold on the {second|third|first} pass. Whatever it is masses far less than it should and comes up easily for {six|five|seven} kilometres.
At six kilometres it stops coming, and the winch keeps running, and the cable keeps paying in.

a1.text: The dock takes the capsule like it was built for it, because it was. Inside there is air, and gravity, and a single corridor with a door at the end of it, and the door opens for {leader} and for {nobody|no one} else.

a2.text: Two hundred frames of a floating city that {nobody|no one} will believe, and a rise back through {hazard} that takes {many} hours and costs a heat shield.

b1.text: The capsule goes past its rating on the way to finding out what the column stands on. It comes back up with {two ports crazed|both ports crazed}, one crew member's ribs gone, and the answer, which {nobody|no one} has been able to write down.

b2.text: The sample arm comes back with three grams of the column in the pot, and the pot weighs {many} kilos, {and it is still cooling|and it has not finished cooling}.

c1.text: What comes up on the end of the cable is {not what the grapple took hold of|nothing like what the grapple took hold of}.

c2.text: The cutter takes the cable and the capsule goes up {like a cork|the way a cork goes up}. Snagged in the last metre of cable, still attached, is a plate of something that will not scratch.

n0.text:
The heat here is enough to end an unprotected argument in {under a second|less than a second}, and the signal is coming from the hottest point on the survey.
Whatever is transmitting is not sheltering from {hazard}. {It is using it.|It is running on it.}

choices.text: Go in with the suit at full cooling.
Send the drone in and stay out.

a.text:
{many} minutes of endurance, and at the end of it, in the middle of {place}, there is a shape that the heat is going around.
It is aware of the away team. It has been waiting for the temperature to bring {somebody|someone}.

choices.text: Get out while the suit still holds.

b.text:
The drone lasts {few} minutes, which is three and a half more than expected, and sends back a picture of {remnant} standing in the fire, unmarked.
Then something takes the drone. Gently. The signal ends without breaking up.

choices.text: Go and get the drone back.

c.text:
The cool phase comes {many} hours later and lasts {lots} minutes, and the team walks in over ground that is merely lethal.
The source is a cavity, and the cavity is lined, and the lining is not natural.

a1.text: The glove does not burn. Something is put into it, {deliberately|on purpose}, by something with no hands, and {leader} walks out of the heat carrying an object that is cold.

a2.text: The suit holds all the way out and fails in the airlock, which is {the best possible place|the one good place} for a suit to fail. The scans taken on the way are worth the replacement.

b1.text: The drone is at the edge of the heat, {set down facing outwards|set down with its face turned outwards}, with its recorder full and its casing packed with something that should not exist at that temperature.

b2.text: The loss goes in the log with the rest of the year's losses. The {few} minutes of footage get {quietly|without fuss} copied by three separate people before the ship reaches the next system.

c1.text: It peels off in sheets, {light as foil|as light as foil}, and every sheet holds temperature like it has an opinion about it. There is enough here to line a ship.

c2.text: The cavity is occupied, and the cool phase is not a phase. {It is a habit|It is a habit of the place}, and the away team has just walked into the middle of it.

n0.text:
There are {many} ships here, moored to {place} in a neat row, all of them different, none of them from any registry the ship carries.
They are not wrecks. They are parked, and {somebody|someone} swept {ground} between them.

choices.text: Find out who does the sweeping.

a.text:
The oldest is stone, or something that has become stone, and its hatch is a hole cut {by hand|by somebody's hand} from the outside.
The inside is one room, {and the room is a nest|and the room has been made into a nest}, and it has been used since long after the ship stopped flying.

choices.text: Wait outside for whatever lives there.

b.text:
The newest has been here {many} years by its own clock and its hull is in better order than the party's own ship.
The crew log ends {on the day they arrived|the day they arrived|on their day of arrival}, mid-sentence, in the middle of a supply count.

choices.text: Try to bring the ship back up.

c.text:
The sweeping is done {at a set hour|to a set hour|on the hour, every time}, and the away team is in cover for it.
What comes out to sweep is small, and old, and does the whole anchorage in {ninety minutes|an hour and a half}, and stops at each ship to check the mooring line.

choices.text: Offer it a mooring line of your own.

a1.text: Under the bedding there are {few} hundred small objects, {sorted by size|graded by size|laid out by size}, and every one of them came off a different ship. The best of them is the last one in the row.

a2.text: {It comes home at the end of its round|It comes back at the end of its round} and it is not pleased to find the door open.

b1.text: {many} years of stores, packed by people who {knew what they were doing|knew the work}, and the away team takes as much as the lander will lift.

b2.text:
The reactor lights on the {third|second|fourth} try and the ship comes up all the way, every board green, {and then|then|and after that} it will not release the moorings, and nothing on any panel explains why.
It is put back to sleep. It goes willingly.

c1.text: It takes the line, tests it, coils it {properly|correctly}, and moors the lander with it, {and then|then|and after that} it hands {leader} the thing it has been carrying since the first ship arrived.

c2.text: Home is a hole under the anchorage, and inside it is every mooring line that has ever failed, {spliced back together|spliced whole again}, and the tools that did the splicing.

n0.text:
The mass is wrong. The body is the size the catalogue says and weighs a third of what it should, and the survey pulse comes back off an inside face.
There is a way in at {place}: a shaft, straight, cut, with {remnant} at the collar.

choices.text: Blow the shaft wider and send the drone.

a.text:
{few} hundred metres of shaft, {and then|then|and after that} it opens out. The inside of the body is a single space with a floor curving up on all sides, and it is not empty.
There is weather in here. There should not be weather in here.

choices.text: Keep to the wall and map it.

b.text:
Sounding takes {a day|a whole day|two days} and turns up the shape of it: chambers, and passages between chambers, and one chamber that returns nothing at all, {as though the pulse goes in and stays|as though the pulse goes in and does not come out}.
{wrongness}.

c.text: The charge opens the collar and the drone goes down with the light on. It sends back {many} minutes of an interior {nobody|no one} will ever be allowed to visit, {and then|then|and after that} its telemetry ends mid-frame, without any of the usual warnings.

a1.text: At the middle is the thing the whole body was built around, hanging at the centre of gravity, {turning slowly|turning, slowly|turning at a walking pace}, and it lets {leader} take one piece of itself without any argument at all.

a2.text: The map takes {six|five|eight} hours and is worth every minute: a complete interior survey of an artificial world, with the machinery of it laid bare along the wall like an anatomy.

b1.text: {It is not a chamber.|That is not a chamber.} It is an occupant, and it has been folded into that space for longer than the body has been in this orbit, and it unfolds.

b2.text: {The answering chambers are stores|The chambers that answered are stores}, and the stores are full, and whoever packed them expected to come back for them.

c1.text: The drone is {lots} metres down, undamaged, and pointing back up the shaft. Something set it down {carefully|with care}, and put something next to it, and left.

c2.text: {many} minutes of the inside of a hollow world sells for {what a small moon sells for|the price of a small moon}. The buyer does not give a name and does not haggle, which is its own kind of answer.

n0.text:
The signal is the away team's own suit telemetry, five channels, correct headers, correct crew names, and it is being received from {place} {many} minutes before the away team lands there.
{leader} lands anyway.

choices.text: Set up and wait for them to arrive.
Talk to them on the suit channel.

a.text:
The tracks are the away team's own boots, in the away team's own sizes, laid down in {ground} before the lander touched.
They lead away from the landing site, do everything the team is about to do, and stop.

choices.text: Do something the tracks did not do.

b.text:
{They arrive on schedule|They arrive exactly on schedule}, from the direction the telemetry said, five of them, in the same suits, walking the way the away team walks.
They stop {lots} metres out and wait to be spoken to.

choices.text: Do not let them any closer.

c.text:
The channel is open both ways and the voice on it is {leader}'s, half a second early, getting every word right before it is said.
It asks the away team not to come to {place}. It is {very|remarkably} calm about it.

a1.text: Where they stop there is a cache, packed by people {with the same hands|whose hands were the same as theirs}, and a note in {leader}'s handwriting that says only: it is worth it, take it, do not stay.

a2.text:
{leader} sits down in {ground} and refuses to move for {few} minutes, out of spite.
It works. The tracks stop being ahead of them. Everything since landing has to be done again, {properly|correctly}, and the team is tired in a way sleep does not touch.

b1.text: They trade fairly, and hard, and they know {exactly|precisely} what the team can spare, which is the most frightening thing about the whole exchange.

b2.text: {They come closer.|They come closer than that.}

c1.text: It tells them. It takes {four|three|five} minutes and the team does not go, and on the walk back the voice thanks them, once, and stops half a second before it should.

c2.text: At {place} there is nothing but {remnant} and a {very|remarkably} clear view, and everybody comes back, and the count is right, and the ship's log will record that the count was right.

n0.text:
The signal is a transponder, ship-standard, on a frequency {nobody|no one} has used in decades, and it is moving. Slowly, over {ground}, in a line that will cross the away team's path.
It stops when the team stops. It has done this before.

choices.text: Set an ambush and wait for it.
Circle round and come at it from behind.

a.text:
{Two hours|Three hours|An hour and a half} in cover at {place}. The transponder comes on at last light and it is being carried, not worn, by something the size of a lander leg that moves {like it has all the time in the world|as though nothing is chasing it}.
It is dragging a net, and the net is full.

choices.text: Let it pass and follow the net.

b.text:
{Coming at it from behind works|Coming up behind it works}, in that the team gets to see it before it sees them.
It is sitting in a scrape it has made for itself, and it is surrounded by suit helmets, arranged in a circle, {all facing inwards|every one facing inwards}.

c.text:
{leader} keys the old frequency and says the standard hail.
The answer is the standard reply, word perfect, in {leader}'s own voice, and it is coming from {about|something like|roughly} sixty metres away.

a1.text: {The first shot is good|The first shot goes exactly where it should} and does nothing at all except make it put the net down.

a2.text: It drags the net to a cache under an overhang and {stows it with the others|puts it away with the others}. There are {lots} years of others. The team lifts one and is gone before it comes back.

b1.text: There is a name {stencilled|stencilled in paint} inside the helmet and a recorder still in the collar with {many} seconds on it. Getting out with both is the hardest walking anyone does that year.

b2.text: {Nobody|No one} speaks until the lander hatch is shut. The transponder is still moving out there, and the ship logs the position, and marks the whole hemisphere as {a place to not go back to|somewhere nobody returns to}.

c1.text:
{Three|Four|Two} exchanges and it runs out of recorded phrases and starts making its own, badly, and the badness is what everybody remembers.
It leaves. It leaves a thing behind, on {ground}, halfway between.

c2.text: It has been waiting {a long time|a good while|longer than anybody says} for {somebody|someone} to walk towards it.

n0.text:
{place} holds a town. Not a camp, not an outpost: streets, drains, a square, and {remnant} at the middle of it where a monument would go.
Nothing here has burned and nothing has fallen. They simply stopped, and {leader} is the first thing to walk these streets in a {very|remarkably} long time.

a.text:
It is a hall, and it is full of seats facing a stage, and on the stage is a machine that has been running the same {six|four|nine} seconds of something for as long as it has had power.
{Every seat is occupied.|Every seat in the hall is occupied.} They are not bodies. They are the shapes bodies leave in a room that has not been disturbed.

choices.text: Play the machine to the end.

b.text:
The drains are {dry, walkable|dry and walkable}, and better built than the streets above them. {Two hundred|Three hundred|A hundred and fifty} metres in they stop being drains and start being a corridor.
{sound}, from further along.

choices.text: Turn back and seal the entrance.

c.text:
{The square is a record.|The square itself is the record.} Every flat surface carries names, and the names are in columns, and the columns are dated, and the dates stop.
{leader} works out the last column is not a list of the dead. It is a rota.

choices.text: Find out what they were taking turns at.

a1.text: It takes {nine|seven|eleven} minutes. It is a message, and it is an apology, and at the end of it the seats are empty in a way they were not before, and everybody in the away team feels it happen.

a2.text: It comes off the stage in {few} pieces and every piece is worth more than the lander. The hall is {very|remarkably} quiet on the way out, and the seats are still occupied.

b1.text: The corridor ends at a door that was locked from this side, by hand, {in a hurry|and in a hurry}, and whatever they locked in has had a {very|remarkably} long time to get used to the idea.

b2.text: The charge brings the roof down {neatly|cleanly|square} across the corridor mouth. On the walk back up, the team lifts a plate of worked metal out of the drain wall: a street sign, or a prayer.

c1.text: Whatever needed watching is under the square, it is still there, and the last name on the rota {never got relieved|was never relieved}. The team relieves them, in the only way left, and takes the post's kit up.

c2.text: {many} thousand names in the ship's archive, none of which can be pronounced. {Somebody|Someone} in the crew starts reading them out loud on the trip home, and does not stop.

n0.text:
At {place} there is a structure that nothing on this world could have made and nothing on this world has touched. It is kept. Something sweeps {ground} around it clean.
{sound} is coming off it in a pattern that {instrument} insists is a language.

choices.text: Leave something of your own on the step.
Survey it from outside and touch nothing.

a.text:
The inside is one room and the room is much larger than the outside allows. The far wall is {a long way off|further off than it can be} and there is a queue of {maker} standing at it, with their backs turned, in perfect order.
They have been standing there long enough to have worn {grooves|hollows} into the floor.

choices.text: Take something from the wall and run.

b.text:
{leader} puts a ration tin on the step, because it is what there is.
The tin is gone before the team has walked ten paces, and in its place, arranged with care, is a set of tools that are the right size for hands {nobody|no one} aboard has.

choices.text: Leave them and put down something better.

c.text:
Three hours of instrument work from {lots} metres out. The structure has no seams, no foundations, and a mass that changes depending on which way it is measured from.
On the way back, {leader} finds a track in {ground} that goes round the whole site. It is fresh.

a1.text: {leader} stands in line for what the suit clock calls {few} minutes and the crew above calls six hours. At the front there is a slot, and whatever is on the other side of it takes one memory and leaves something in its place.

a2.text: {The queue turns around all|The whole queue turns around all} {at once|all at the same time|together}, and none of them are facing the way faces should face.

b1.text: They come apart and go together in ways the ship's workshop will be arguing about for months. Two of them are missing a use {nobody|no one} has found yet.

b2.text:
The second offering is {a photograph|a photograph out of somebody's locker}, which is the most expensive thing anyone is carrying.
What comes back for it is not an object. It is a length of quiet in the middle of the away team, and everybody who walks through it comes out of it well.

c1.text: The track goes round the site nine times {and then|then|and after that} straight out to a cache buried {a metre|two metres|a half-metre} down, packed and labelled by whoever does the sweeping, as though for collection.

c2.text: The survey is the most valuable document the ship has filed all year, and it will be argued over by people who were not there. {Nothing follows the lander up.|Nothing comes up after the lander.}

n0.text:
It is not a distress call. It is {tone}, and it has been going out from {place} for {a|as long as the catalogue has entries for this system|longer than the catalogue admits}.
{leader} takes it down to the source. The count does not change when the away team arrives, which somehow makes it worse.

choices.text: Answer it in the same pattern.
Find the transmitter and open it.

a.text:
{leader} keys the pattern back, one beat late, {deliberately|on purpose} wrong in the last place.
The count stops. Nine seconds later it starts again, corrected, and now it is answering the mistake rather than repeating itself.

choices.text: Shut the radio off and back away.

b.text:
The transmitter is buried in {ground} with only its collar showing, and the collar is a hatch. It opens by hand. It was built to open by hand.
Inside: a mechanism with no moving parts, and {remnant} laid neatly on top of it, like an offering.

choices.text: Take the offering and close the hatch.

c.text:
The jammer goes up on a tripod and the band flattens out. For {many} minutes there is nothing across the whole spectrum but the sound of the away team breathing.
Then {hazard} makes itself felt, and the count comes back at three times the power.

choices.text: Hold the position and burn it out.

a1.text: It takes {few} hours to build a shared count and another two to trade nouns. What is on the other end is not close, is not alive in any sense the team can use, and gives {leader} a set of coordinates as a gift for the trouble.

a2.text: {The radio goes dark.|The radio goes dead.} The count keeps on over {ground} behind them all the way back to the lander, and the team walks the last hundred metres faster than they walked the first.

b1.text: {It lifts out easily.|It lifts out without any trouble.} The count stops, and every instrument the away team is carrying reports the same time to the same tenth of a second for the first time since they left Earth.

b2.text: The hatch shuts {sweetly|cleanly|the way it should}, the way a well-made thing does. The count carries on, and the team goes up with something in a bag that {nobody|no one} has a word for yet.

c1.text: The jammer wins, {eventually|in the end|sooner or later}, and the source dies with a noise like {a held breath let go|a breath finally let out}. The team digs the emitter out of the slag afterwards: it is beautiful, and it is worth a fortune.

c2.text: Whatever the count belongs to gets to the lander {before the team does|ahead of the team}, and it is standing between them and the hatch when they come over the last rise.

n0.text:
There are machines here and they are busy. Thousands of them, none bigger than a hand, moving over {ground} at {place} on a job that has {clearly|plainly} been running for centuries.
They ignore the away team {completely|utterly|altogether}, which is not the same as not noticing them.

choices.text: Work out what they are building.

a.text:
Two hours of watching and the pattern comes clear. They are not building. They are taking something apart, {very|remarkably} slowly, {very|remarkably} {carefully|with care}, and putting the pieces in order along a line that runs to the horizon.
The thing being taken apart is the world.

choices.text: Follow the line to the far end.
Take a piece off the line.

b.text:
It comes up in a glove {without a fight|without any argument}, folds its legs, and goes still.
Every other machine within sight stops at the same instant, and stays stopped, {and turns to face the glove|and every one of them turns to face the glove}.

c.text:
{leader} sets a sample case down across their line and steps back.
The swarm stops at it, considers it for nine seconds, {and then|then|and after that} goes round. On the way past, one of them measures the case and writes the measurement on it.

choices.text: Take the case back and leave them to it.

a1.text: The far end is a stack, sorted by material, {taller than the lander|higher than the lander}, and at the top of it is the first thing they ever took off this world, labelled in a notation that predates the swarm.

a2.text: The line closes the gap in {many} seconds and does not react otherwise. The piece is a machined block of something the ship's assay cannot name, and there are {few} hundred kilometres of them.

b1.text: The moment it touches {ground} the whole field goes back to work {as though nothing happened|as though nothing at all had happened}. Where it was standing there is now a small object that was not there before, and it is a gift, or a receipt.

b2.text: {few} hundred metres from the lander the field decides how it feels about theft.

c1.text: The cutter goes down on the line. They swarm it, measure it, take it apart, and put it back together {improved|better than it was}, and leave it on {ground} pointing at the lander.

c2.text: The case comes back with a number on it in a base {nobody|no one} uses, {and the swarm carries on|and the swarm goes back to work}, and the away team is up and gone before anybody has to find out what the number means.

n0.text:
{hour} the swell flattens out for no reason anyone can give, and a hull comes up out of it: a fishing boat, riding high, nets still out and {nobody|no one} on the deck.
The name has been painted over {twice|two separate times}. Under both coats it is the same name.

choices.text: Haul in the nets from your own side.
Circle her once and log the position.

a.text:
{The galley kettle is warm.|The kettle in the galley is still warm.} The log is written up to this morning in {a steady hand|an unhurried hand|a hand that was not rushed}, and the last line is a list of everyone aboard with a tick against every name.
Below that, in the same hand: they all came back.

choices.text: Take the log and search the hold.
Answer the tick with your own names.

b.text:
The net comes up {heavy and wrong|heavy, and wrong with it}, the weight shifting {the way weight does when it is deciding|the way a weight shifts when it has a mind of its own}.
{leader} braces on the rail and gets it over the side.

choices.text: Put it back in the water.

c.text:
Two turns, close in, and the boat drifts the whole time against the current instead of with it.
The crew notes the heading, the hour and the fact that the deck is dry in a rain that has not stopped since dawn, and leaves her to it. A fortnight later the sighting is worth something to a {very|remarkably} quiet office in {region}.

a1.text: The hold is full of ice and under the ice is the catch of a season {nobody|no one} had. Packed in the middle of it, wrapped in oilcloth {like the best fish aboard|the way the best fish aboard is wrapped}, is a thing that was never in any sea.

a2.text:
The pen is where the last hand left it. Everyone signs, {because it seems rude not to|because not signing seems rude}, and the boat leans very slightly towards the party as they do.
What comes up the companionway wants its list back.

b1.text: {Sailcloth, cable, three crates of ship's stores|Sailcloth, cable, and three crates of stores} and a sounding weight of good bronze. Whoever lost this net lost {a working month|a month's work|a season's work} with it.

b2.text:
It goes down slower than it should, keeping its shape, and something takes it {politely|civilly} at {about|something like|roughly} {few} fathoms.
The swell picks back up. Everyone aboard sleeps that night like they have not slept in a year.

n0.text:
A square of the crop is still standing in a field that was cut a month ago, and it is standing in a shape: {lots} paces across, sides too straight for a plough.
Inside it {sound_field}. Outside it, nothing at all.

choices.text: Walk into the middle of it.
Cut a sheaf and take it away.

a.text:
The stalks {bend away|lean away|part} as the party comes on and close again behind them, and in the centre there is a patch of bare, packed earth with a hollow in it the size of {a sleeping animal|a sleeping dog|something that sleeps curled up}. It is warm.
The crop around the hollow has grown a second time this year, out of season, and it has grown heavy.

b.text:
The farmhouse is a mile off and the man there does not want to talk about the square. He wants to talk about his father, who left it standing for {lots} years, and about what the two dry summers were like the once it got cut.
He will pay for it to be left alone. He will pay more if someone will go and look.

choices.text: Take his money and leave the square standing.
Take his tools and cut it flat.

c.text:
The sheaf comes away easily and stays green for {many} days in a pack where bread goes mouldy in three.
The grain in it is heavier than the grain around it and it seeds true. The agricultural office in {region} takes the whole sheaf and asks no questions worth answering.

a1.text: It is the length of a person and it fits like it was measured. {leader} is out for {many} minutes by the watch and wakes up with a taste of copper, a scar closed that has been open since spring, and everybody standing over them looking rested for the first time in a month.

a2.text: {A foot down|Two feet down|Half a spade down}, the earth stops being earth. What comes up out of the hollow has been sleeping there through several harvests and it wants {the rest of its year|the rest of the year it is owed}.

b1.text:
He pays in the notes his father kept back from {three|two|four} good years and shakes every hand {twice|two separate times}.
The square is still standing. Everything around it will be, too.

b2.text:
It cuts like any crop and threshes out at {few} times what the field beside it gave. {The sacks go on the cart|The sacks go up on the cart} and the farmer will not touch them, so they go with the party instead.
He stands at the gate watching the flat ground and does not wave anyone off.

n0.text:
{many} hives in a meadow with no house within a day's walk, painted and re-painted and kept, and the grass between them is mown.
The bees are working {weather}, which bees do not do.

choices.text: Wait for whoever mows the grass.
Take a comb from the outermost hive and go.

a.text:
The comb is built around something that is not a frame: {a rod of dark metal|a dark metal rod|a length of dark metal}, set upright in the middle of the brood, and the whole colony has organised itself around it as though it were the queen.
{They do not sting.|Nothing stings.} They move aside.

choices.text: Close the hive and leave everything as it was.

b.text:
{Nobody|No one} comes. At dusk the mowing {starts anyway|begins anyway|starts regardless}, a long way off at first, working inward in {neat lines|tidy lines} that nothing is standing in.
By full dark the grass around the party's boots is cut.

choices.text: Stand still and let it finish.
Get between it and the hives.

c.text:
It is the best honey anyone aboard has had, and there is nine kilos of it, and the hive is fuller the next morning than it was before the comb came out.
{Nobody|No one} says anything about going back for more. Everybody thinks it.

a1.text: It is warm at one end and it hums against the palm at the pitch the hive hums at. The colony goes quiet for {exactly|precisely} as long as it takes to walk out of the meadow, {and then|then|and after that} goes back to work on nothing.

a2.text: {The lid goes back down and the hum comes back up to where it was|The lid goes back and the hum settles to where it was}. Something in the meadow is satisfied, and the party's water bottles are full and cold when they get back to them, and one of the packs has a wax-sealed jar in it that {nobody|no one} put there.

b1.text: It goes round the party's feet and moves on without touching them. In the morning there is a scythe {laid across the path out|set across the path out}, old, sharp, the handle worn to fit a hand that is very nearly a hand.

b2.text: {It does not stop for the hives|It does not stop at the hives} and it does not stop for {anyone standing in front of them|anybody standing in front of them}.

n0.text:
{A hunter's blind|A shooting blind|A high seat}, nailed up a beech at the height of a first branch, in a wood with no track to it. {The ladder is new.|The ladder has been replaced this year.} The rifle rest is worn shiny.
It is facing away from the deer path, and it is facing {landmark}.

choices.text: Climb up and sit in it.
Follow the sightline to what it is watching.
Strip it for what it is worth.

a.text:
There is a flask, a cushion, and a tally cut into the rail: three hundred and {many} marks, in groups of {few} struck through, made over years by someone patient.
Nothing on the ground has been shot. There are no bones under this tree.

choices.text: Sit the watch out until dark.
Cut a mark of your own into the rail.

b.text:
{Ninety|Eighty|A hundred and twenty} paces along the sightline the wood opens onto a clearing that is not on any map, and in the middle of it is a stone with a hollow ground into the top of it.
{The hollow has been kept filled.|Something has kept the hollow filled.} Whatever was in it this morning is gone.

choices.text: Fill it from your own stores.

c.text:
The rifle rest is machined, the ladder is good ash and the flask is silver under {a century|a hundred years|four generations} of thumbing.
On the walk out, every bird in the wood starts up {at once|all at the same time|together}, and behind the party something comes down the ladder they have just taken.

a1.text: At last light the wood goes quiet in a ring that {closes on the tree|shuts in around the tree}, and holds, and opens again on nothing. Whatever it was walked under the blind and left what it was carrying at the foot of it, {the way you would pay a toll|the way a toll gets paid}.

a2.text:
{The knife goes in easily.|The knife takes the bark without argument.} Three hundred and twelve.
Something in the wood has been counting too, and the number is a promise, and {leader} has just made it on everybody's behalf.

b1.text:
{Salt, a strip of meat and the last of the good bread|Salt, dried meat, and what is left of the good bread}. It is gone before the party is out of the clearing.
The wood lets them out on the side they wanted, which is not the side they walked in on, and every scratch anybody took today is {shut|closed over}.

b2.text:
Under the stone the ground is packed with what has been paid over a {very|remarkably} long time: coin from {few} countries, teeth, buttons, a wedding band, a cartridge case still in its wax.
The wood does not stop them. It simply never lets any of them enjoy a clearing again.

n0.text:
{A stand of black spruce|A thicket of black spruce}, and standing in it, upright and frozen through, an elk that has been dead since some winter {nobody|no one} can date. The snow around it is undisturbed to a radius of {ten|eight|twelve} paces.
Nothing has taken a bite out of it. In this country, in this cold, that is the strange part.

choices.text: Camp beside it and watch what comes.
Leave it and follow its tracks backwards.

a.text:
{The hide is board-hard|The hide is stiff as board} and the meat under it is fresh, red, and the wrong temperature: not frozen, not warm, {exactly|precisely} nothing.
The heart is missing and the cavity has been packed with clean snow by {something with hands|something that has hands}.

choices.text: Pack it back up the way you found it.

b.text:
The cold comes down to a place where the fire stops meaning anything. At the {third|fourth|second} hour something crosses the clearing at the edge of the light, on two legs, tall, and stops at the elk and stands with it.
{It is keeping it.|It is minding it.} It has kept it for {a long time|a good while|longer than anybody says}.

choices.text: Offer it a share of the fire.

c.text:
The tracks run backwards for {few} miles under new snow, which is not possible, and end at a hollow in the roots of a windfall where {somebody|someone} lived through a winter on {very|remarkably} little.
The kit left in there is old, and it is good, and the man who owned it did not need it after all.

a1.text: It feeds everybody for {a week|nine days|a fortnight} and it does not spoil and {nobody|no one} who eats it is cold again for a month, in any weather, which is worth more up here than the meat is.

a2.text:
Snow, hide, and the wound closed with a splint of green wood, {as neatly as it can be done by firelight|as neatly as firelight allows}.
In the morning the party's packs are heavier by {a good weight|a considerable weight} of dressed fur, and the elk is gone, and the ten paces of unmarked snow are unmarked still.

b1.text: It sits down at the edge of the light and stays until the wood goes grey. It does not eat. When it goes it leaves the heart of the elk in the snow at {leader}'s boots, thawed, and warm, and beating twice more before it stops.

b2.text: {It is fast for something|It is quick for a thing} that has been standing still {since the last ice age|since the ice went}.

n0.text:
{lots} metres up, in the crown of a fig, there is a platform: plank, rope, tin roof, a rainwater butt, all of it {lots} years old and none of it rotten in a forest that eats a felled tree in two seasons.
The ladder starts eight metres off the ground.

choices.text: Search the base of the tree.

a.text:
Someone lived up here for years: notebooks in a language {nobody|no one} reads, jars of specimens, a hammock, a rifle with no rounds left, and a chart of the canopy that maps {many} trees and marks one of them with a cross.
The crossed tree is visible from the rail. Something is moving in it.

b.text:
The roots are staked out with {pegs and string|string and pegs} in a grid, and each square of the grid has been dug and filled back in. The last {three|two|four} are still open.
In the bottom of the last one is a hand's worth of yellow metal that came out of this ground, not out of a river.

choices.text: Dig the rest of the grid.
Fill them in and mark the site on your own chart.

c.text:
{Nobody|No one} answers. Everything else does: the whole forest goes up {at once|all at the same time|together}, howlers and macaws and something under it all with a lower voice, and it stays up for {few} minutes and stops dead.
On the ground at the party's feet, dropped from a great height, is a satchel of instruments still in working order.

a1.text: {lots} years of a life spent looking at one hectare. {Six|Four|Five} universities want it and the one that gets it pays in a currency that spends anywhere.

a2.text: {The rope holds.|The rope holds, which is the last piece of luck in it.} The tree does not want the party in it, and it has been keeping something up there {since before the platform was built|since before there was a platform}.

b1.text: {few} more squares and the seam gives it up: worked gold, not ore, {hammered flat and folded over|beaten flat and folded} and buried by people who buried it to keep it out of somebody's hands.

b2.text:
The pegs go back, the string goes back, the earth goes back. The forest closes it in a fortnight and the coordinates are worth {exactly|precisely} what the party decides they are worth, later, in a room in {region}.
Something watches the whole job from the canopy and lets them walk out.

n0.text:
There is a light in the trees, at head height, at the distance where it never gets closer. It has been there since before the party came in, because everyone here has a story about it from before they came in.
{leader} counts the trees between here and there. The count comes out different every time.

choices.text: Walk out of the wood by the way you came.

a.text:
It backs off at a walking pace for three hours {and then|then|and after that} it doesn't, and it is a lamp, an ordinary storm lamp, hung on a branch at head height with the wick trimmed and the oil half gone.
Under it there is {a good deal|a great deal|rather a lot} of ground that has been walked flat by people arriving.

choices.text: Fill it from your own oil and leave it burning.

b.text:
In the dark the wood is not the wood. {There are two of everything|Everything in here has a second of itself} and one of them is closer, and the light in the trees is much nearer than it has been letting on.
{It is not a light.|That is not a light.} It is an opening, and the light is what is on the other side of it.

c.text:
The way back is {exactly|precisely} as long as it was and comes out where it should, which in this wood is a courtesy, not a certainty.
Everybody's watch is {few} minutes fast. Whatever that was worth, the party did not spend it.

a1.text:
It comes down easily and it goes out, and the wood is suddenly a wood, ordinary and cold, and the way home is {fifteen|twenty|ten} minutes east.
{The lamp does not light again for anyone.|Nobody gets the lamp to light again.} It is also not empty, and what is in it is not oil, and a certain kind of buyer knows that at a glance.

a2.text:
{The wick takes.|The wick catches first time.} The light steadies, and settles, and stops being a thing that moves away.
Walking out, every member of the party is given back something they had lost in here: {a knife, an hour, a name|a knife, an hour, a name they had mislaid} they had been trying for days to remember.

b1.text: It is warm on the other side, and bright, and there are people at a table who make room. {Nobody|No one} can say afterwards what was said. Everybody comes back out of the same tree they went in at, {lots} minutes later, carrying something they were given.

b2.text: {Dawn takes|First light takes} {a long time|a good while|longer than anybody says} and it is not alone in here waiting for it.

n0.text:
A cairn on the saddle, chest-high, and it is built out of stone that does not come from this mountain. {Somebody|Someone} carried every piece of it up.
On the flat capstone {somebody|someone} has left {offering}, out of the wind, dry.

choices.text: Add a stone and go on.
Wait beside it for the weather to turn.

a.text:
{The stone goes on and settles|The stone goes on the cairn and settles}, and the wind drops out of the saddle entirely, which anyone who has walked this country knows does not happen.
In the lee of it the path onward is {suddenly obvious|suddenly plain to see}, and it is not the path the party would have taken.

choices.text: Take the path it is showing you.

b.text:
{Three|Four|Two} courses down there is a slate box, and in the box a rolled sheet, and on the sheet a list of names in the same hand as the map that comes with it.
{The map is of this mountain.|The map is this mountain.} There is one mark on it that is not a summit and not a hut.

choices.text: Rebuild the cairn and take the map.

c.text:
{It turns hard within the hour|The weather turns hard inside the hour}, and the cairn is a poor shelter but it is the only one, and the party sits it out in the lee of a thing built by {somebody|someone} who sat out the same weather.
They come off the mountain a day late and entirely alive, which the mountain does not always allow.

a1.text: It contours round to a ledge {nobody|no one} could see from the saddle, and on the ledge is a pack, {lots} years old, belonging to someone who did not come back and who packed {very|remarkably} well.

a2.text: The planned route goes fine for two hours {and then|then|and after that} the cloud comes down on it. Everybody gets off the hill. Everybody is {a good deal|a great deal|rather a lot} worse for it, and {nobody|no one} says out loud what they are all thinking about the cairn.

b1.text:
It is a cleft under an overhang, and the people on the list are all in it, laid out in order, with everything they were carrying stacked at their feet where {somebody|someone} put it for them.
They have been waiting {a long time|a good while|longer than anybody says} for someone to come up and take it down.

b2.text:
Every stone goes back where it came from, and it takes {until dark|until the light goes|the rest of the day}, and the box goes back with the sheet in it and the map goes in {leader}'s coat.
The mountain lets the party down in weather that has no business being this kind.

n0.text:
The glacier has opened a crevasse across the route, and {eight|ten|six} metres down, held in the blue like something in a jar, there is a rope. {It is running.|The rope is running.} It goes into the ice on one side and out of it on the other.
Someone is on the end of it and has been for a {very|remarkably} long time.

choices.text: Cut it and take what comes up.
Bridge the crevasse and go on.

a.text:
{It is cold in a way that is a sound.|The cold down here has a sound to it.} At {twelve|fourteen|ten} metres the rope runs into a wall of ice with a shape behind it, close enough to see the wool of the jersey, the ice axe, the face.
The face is turned up towards the party and it was turned up before they got here.

choices.text: Take the axe and leave them in.

b.text:
The rope comes up hand over hand, {lots} metres of it, and at the end there is a knot, and in the knot there is a mitten, and in the mitten there is a hand.
The ice below the party gives {a noise it has not made all day|a noise nothing has made all day}.

choices.text: Drop it and get off the glacier.

c.text:
Ladder, two screws and a {very|remarkably} careful ten minutes. The party crosses, and the rope goes on running in the blue underneath them, and {nobody|no one} looks down {twice|two separate times}.
The route beyond it goes well. It goes better than it should.

a1.text: {few} hours of axe work to bring up someone who has been eighty years in the ice, with their name still legible inside the collar. There are people in {region} who have been waiting on that name for three generations, and they pay what they said they would.

a2.text: The axe comes out of the ice with a crack that {runs the length of the crevasse|goes the whole length of the crevasse}, and the hand that was holding it comes with it, and the crevasse decides it would {like the party to stay|rather the party stayed}.

b1.text: Everything they were carrying comes up with them, packed as {carefully|with care} as a man packs when he expects to need it tomorrow: {a lamp, a set of screws|a lamp, ice screws}, and a case of instruments in brass that still read true.

b2.text:
The glacier takes the rope back at speed and the lip goes where the party was standing {few} seconds earlier.
Everybody gets off. {Two people|One of them|Two of them} get off badly, and the walk out is long.

n0.text:
Cut into the face of the mesa, a stair. Two hundred steps, hand-worked, going up to a ledge with nothing on it, and the rock at the top is worn into a groove by feet.
{Nobody|No one} has lived within {lots} miles of here in living memory.

choices.text: Work along the base looking for the door it belongs to.
Sit at the bottom until the shadow reaches the first step.

a.text:
{The ledge is empty and swept.|The ledge is bare, and swept.} From up here the desert below is not empty at all: there are lines in it, straight, miles long, that cannot be seen from the ground, and they all run to the foot of this stair.
{They are paths.|Those are paths.} They are still being walked.

choices.text: Wait on the ledge for whoever walks them.
Map the lines and get down before dark.

b.text:
{lots} paces round the base the rock has been cut and filled, and the fill is a plug of dressed stone with a hand's grip worn into it, from the inside.
{Something closed this behind itself.|Something shut this behind itself.}

choices.text: Leave it shut and camp against it.

c.text:
The shadow comes off the mesa {at the hour|on the hour|as the hour turns}, and the steps go from bare rock to a stair of shade, and for {about|something like|roughly} ninety seconds there is a sound of people coming down it, unhurried, a great many of them.
They pass. The party has been counted and let alone.

a1.text: At last light they arrive up all {few} paths {at once|all at the same time|together}, and they are courteous, and they do not stay, and each of them leaves at {leader}'s feet the thing they carried up here to leave.

a2.text: {few} lines, {many} miles, three junctions and a centre. The survey is worth money to a university and {a great deal|a good deal|rather a lot} more to a mining company, and only one of the two is told.

b1.text: The plug comes out into a chamber cut level with a floor of {laid stone|dressed stone}, and stacked on it is what a people carried up here when they went in for the last time and {pulled the door shut after them|shut the door after themselves}.

b2.text:
It is a good wall to have at your back and a poor one to sleep against. Something works at the fill from inside all night, {patiently|without hurry}, and stops at first light with the plug a finger's width out.
Everybody is alive. {Nobody|No one} rested.

n0.text:
The sand has moved off a line of vehicles: {six|five|seven} trucks, nose to tail, tyres flat, canvas gone, the paint sandblasted down to bare metal on the windward side and perfect on the other.
{The fuel caps are all open.|Every fuel cap is off.} The tanks are all full.

a.text:
{No drivers, no bodies, no boots.|No drivers, no bodies, not a boot between them.} Every cab has the keys in it and the handbrake off, and the lead truck has a map on the seat with a route on it that ends here, in the middle of nothing, marked as a destination.
{Somebody|Someone} drove six trucks to a place and got out and walked.

b.text:
Five beds are empty and swept. The sixth is full of crates, stencilled in a hand {nobody|no one} uses any more, and the top one is open, and whatever came out of it was taken out {carefully|with care}.
The rest are sealed.

choices.text: Take a sealed crate whole and leave the rest.

c.text: Eight hundred litres of fuel that should have gone to varnish {lots} years ago and has not. {It burns clean, it moves anything|It burns clean and it will move anything}, and it sells for what it is: impossible, and useful.

a1.text:
They go out {a mile and a half|a mile|two miles} in a straight line and stop. Not scattered, not covered: stopped, all of them, at the same point, facing the same way.
What is buried at that point is not a body. {It is much older than the trucks|It is a great deal older than the trucks}, and it is the reason they drove here.

a2.text: {It starts. Of course it starts.|It starts, which nobody in the party wanted.} It also does not stop, and it has been waiting for a driver, and it {did not specify|never specified} which one it would take.

b1.text: {Machine parts in grease|Spares packed in grease}, tools in oil paper, spare barrels, and a crate of rations that are still, by {any test anyone can run out here|every test anybody can run out here}, food.

b2.text: It takes {few} of them to carry it and it goes in the hold unopened, and it stays unopened for a fortnight, and a dealer in {region} pays for it unopened, which is the sort of price a man only offers when he knows {exactly|precisely} what is in it.

n0.text:
{Rain|A wet fortnight|The spring melt} has cut a new gully through the clay and opened a bed of bone in the side of it, {lots} metres of it, {layered like a wall|banded like brickwork|stacked in courses}.
Most of it is old past reckoning. About a metre of it is not, and that metre has been dug at from below.

choices.text: Get into the hole that was dug from below.
Photograph the face and sell the location.

a.text:
{Two days|A day and a half|Three days} with brushes and {a good deal|a great deal|rather a lot} of care and there is a skull out of it entire, of nothing on any list, with {a hole|a neat hole|a bored hole} through the crown that was made by a tool.
The tool is in the next layer down, and it is not stone.

choices.text: Take the skull and leave the layer sealed.

b.text:
It goes in {three|four|five} metres and opens into a burrow that runs along the bone bed, and the walls of it are packed with bones that have been sorted: long with long, jaw with jaw, skull with skull.
{Something down here files.|Something down here keeps a system.|Something down here sorts what it finds.}

choices.text: Back out and collapse it behind you.

c.text:
The plates are good and the site is genuine and the buyer is {a museum with a bad conscience and a large budget|a university with more money than provenance|a private buyer with a wing to fill}. The gully will be under a tent by {the autumn|September|next season}.
What is in the burrow will be {somebody|someone} else's problem by then.

a1.text: It comes out of clay that has not been open to the air since {long before there was anyone to make a tool|an age before anybody could have made a tool}, and it is machined, and it fits {a hand|the hand|a grip}.

a2.text:
The skull goes into a crate packed with the party's own spare clothes and the layer under it goes back under clay, {tamped and sealed and marked on nobody's map|tamped, sealed, and left off every map there is}.
{The money is good.|The money is better than good.} The sleep afterwards is better.

b1.text: {The sorting gets neater the further in it goes|The order of it improves with every metre}, and the freshest section is the neatest, and it has a gap in it {exactly|precisely} the size of a person.

b2.text:
{Two|Three} charges in the clay and the burrow comes down for its whole visible length, and the noise from underneath goes on for {a while|some minutes|longer than it should} afterwards {and then|then|and after that} does not.
What came out of the mouth of it on the way, half-sorted and worth carrying, goes in the packs.

n0.text:
{A steel stake|A driven steel stake|A survey stake} in the permafrost with a brass cap, stamped with a number and a year that has not happened yet.
There are {five|six|seven} more within a mile, in a line, and the line runs to the horizon in both directions.

choices.text: Take a rubbing and leave the stakes alone.

a.text:
{many} miles of it, {dead straight over ground that has no straight lines in it|arrow-straight across country with nothing straight in it}, and at the end of the line there is a rig: a drill mast, a hut, a fuel bowser, all of it new and none of it started.
{The hut is warm and there is tea in the pot.|The hut is warm, the stove is lit, and the pot has tea in it.}

choices.text: Take what is useful and go.

b.text:
It goes down {two and a half|three|two} metres into ground that a pick will not touch, and it comes out with the bottom end warm, and the hole it leaves is not a hole in soil.
{There is a cavity under this.|There is a void under this.} There is a cavity under all of them.

choices.text: Put the stake back and tamp it.

c.text:
Wax and paper and {many} brass caps recorded, and the numbers on them run in a sequence with three gaps.
{Somebody|Someone} in an office is going to want this {very|remarkably} badly, and the party will be the ones who name the price.

a1.text: They come in at midnight in {two tracked vehicles|a pair of tracked vehicles}, and they are not surprised, and they are {extremely|entirely|thoroughly} glad to see anyone at all. What they have brought up out of the first hole has kept them from starting the second, and they will hand it to anyone who will take it away.

a2.text: {Fuel, cable, a good stove|Fuel, cable, a stove worth the carrying}, two crates of core samples and a set of cold-weather kit that would cost {a season's pay|a whole season's pay} anywhere south of here.

b1.text: The cavity is {a metre|a good metre|four feet} across and it is smooth and it has been kept open, and it goes down further than the lamp goes, and the thing in it is coming up to {see who pulled the stake|find out who pulled the stake}.

b2.text: In it goes, straight and true, and the ground takes it back and closes on it. {Ten|Eight|Twelve} miles on, at the fifth stake, someone has left a case out on the tundra with the party's own heading written on the lid, which is {a wage, and a request|a wage, and also a request}.

n0.text:
A slump in the frozen ground, {ten|eight|fifteen} metres across, where the ice under the soil has let go and taken the surface down with it.
What the thaw has brought up out of the bottom of it has been in there since long before this was tundra, {and it is not all bone|and not all of it is bone}.

choices.text: Take samples from the edge and stay out of it.
Refreeze what you can and mark the site.

a.text: {It smells like a stable and a butcher's and a river bank|It smells of a stable, a butcher's shop, and low water}. {Half|A good third} of a mammoth is out of the wall, and beside it, packed in the same mud, a sledge, and on the sledge a load that was tied down by someone who meant to come back for it.

b.text:
Six cores, and every one of them has something alive in it that has not been alive anywhere else for {lots} thousand years.
{One of the six is still moving in the tube.|One of the six has not stopped moving in the tube.}

choices.text: Open the one that is moving.

c.text:
{Two days|Three days|A day and a night} of hard, cold, unrewarding work: the exposed face packed and covered, the slump edged, a cairn and a plate with a date on it.
It will hold {a decade|ten years|a season or two}, perhaps. {Somebody|Someone} will be glad of the decade.

a1.text: Furs, worked ivory, a bundle of tools in a hide roll and a thing at the bottom wrapped in {many} layers that everyone agrees, without discussing it, {to leave wrapped|to leave exactly as it is}.

a2.text: {Two metres|Two good metres|A full two metres} of ivory, sound the whole way, worth {a year|two years} of anybody's wages. The mud comes off it and the mud does not want to leave the slump, and neither, it turns out, does what was lying under it.

b1.text:
They go into the cold store double-sealed and they are sold that way, unopened, to the one institute that promised in writing to keep them that way.
{The cheque clears.|The cheque clears on the day it is dated.} {So far, so does the promise.|So far the promise holds too.}

b2.text: {It is out of the tube before the cap is fully off.|It is out of the tube while the seal is still turning.}

n0.text:
On the flank, where the old flow went over the ridge, {a vent is going|a vent is working|a vent is open}: not smoke, a column of clean heat that stands straight up in wind that should be laying it flat.
{Around the mouth of it the rock has been dressed.|The rock round the mouth of it has been dressed square.} {Somebody|Someone} made this a doorway.

choices.text: Follow the flow down to what it buried.
Take a reading from a distance and leave.

a.text:
{Standing at the lip is like standing in front of an open furnace door|Standing at the lip is like standing at the door of a lit furnace} and being looked at through it. The heat holds at {exactly|precisely} the temperature a person can bear, and no closer, and it does that as the party moves.
Set into the dressed stone are handholds, going down.

b.text:
The flow went through a village and stopped in the middle of it, {dead square|square across|clean across}, leaving one half in ash and the other half standing {with the washing still on the lines|with washing still out on the lines}.
The standing half has not been lived in since, and it has not been looted either.

choices.text: Go to the house the flow stopped at.

c.text: Temperature, gas, and a column that reads as no gas at all. The observatory in {region} does not believe the figures and buys them anyway, {twice|two separate times}, once for the record and once to keep it off the record.

a1.text: Nine metres down the handholds end at a floor, and the floor is glass, and under the glass the mountain is {going about its business|getting on with its business} a long way below and something is going about its business in the middle of it, and it stops to acknowledge the party before they climb back out.

a2.text:
{A ration tin, because it is what there is.|A ration tin, for want of anything better.} It goes in and does not fall.
What comes back up the shaft is the same shape as a tin and made of something that took a {very|remarkably} long time to cool, and it is not the only thing coming up.

b1.text: Everything anybody left when they ran, and they ran with what they could carry, which was not much. {Tools, stock, a jeweller's whole stripped bench|Tools, stock, and a jeweller's bench stripped bare}, and in the church box the collection of {a wealthy parish|a very wealthy parish}.

b2.text: {The flow came up to the doorstep and stopped.|The flow reached the doorstep and went no further.} There is a woman's chair in the doorway, still turned to face it, and what she was holding when the mountain {changed its mind|thought better of it} is on the seat.

n0.text:
{Walls to knee height|Walls no higher than a knee|Wall footings and nothing above them}, a gate arch still standing, and a floor of laid stone that has sunk in the middle so {the whole of|all of} it drains to one point.
At that point there is a grating, {and it is clear of leaves, and nothing else here is|and it is swept clean, and nothing else here is}.

choices.text: Walk the walls and read what is cut into them.
Dig the floor at the four corners.

a.text: Under it, {a shaft with rungs, dry|a rung shaft, dry the whole way down}, and at the bottom a room the ruin above has no business having: plastered, painted, the colours still in it, and a long table with places set for a meal that {was not eaten|nobody sat down to|was laid and never served}.

b.text:
{The cutting is a list|What is cut there is a list}, and it runs the length of three walls, and it is a list of what was taken away from here and by whom, in the order it went.
The last line was cut recently, in the same lettering, and it names a road {three|two|four} days from here.

c.text: {Three corners|Two of the corners|Three of the four corners} give up potsherds and a coin. The fourth gives up a jar, sealed with wax and pitch, that has kept a hoard of small silver dry for a {very|remarkably} long time.

a1.text: {The chairs are the right height|The chairs are the right height for whoever sits in them} and the room warms while everybody is sitting in it. {Nobody|No one} eats. Nothing is served. When the party stands up the table is bare and each of them is holding what was in front of them, which was not there when they sat down.

a2.text: {It is silver under the tarnish|Under the tarnish it is silver} and it weighs what a good plate weighs, and it comes up the rungs easily, and something at the table objects to {the place being one short|the table being one short}.

b1.text: There is a carter on that road, on that day, carrying {exactly|precisely} what the wall says he is carrying, and he has been waiting for {somebody|someone} to come and take it off him for {many} years.

b2.text:
{leader} cuts the party's own name and what they came for. It takes {an hour|the best part of an hour|two hours} and the letters come out better than they should.
What is under the grating that night puts something on the top rung for them, and does not come up after it.

n0.text:
In a burying ground where the newest stone is a hundred and {lots} years old, one grave has been opened and filled in again {this week|in the last few days|since Sunday}. {The turf is laid back neatly.|The turf has been laid back with some care.}
There is no stone on it, and there is a spade leaning against the wall, cleaned.

a.text:
{few} feet down the spade rings on wood, and the wood is old, far older than the digging, and it has been opened before and closed again with new nails.
{Somebody|Someone} put something in with the occupant, recently, and did the coffin the courtesy of shutting it {properly|correctly}.

choices.text: Fill it in and lay the turf back as you found it.

b.text:
{The church is locked|The church door is locked} and the register is in the vestry press, and the last entry is in this month's ink: a name, no dates, and in the margin, in the same hand, returned.
The same name appears {many} times, going back {three hundred|four hundred|two hundred} years, always with the same note.

choices.text: Wait in the vestry for whoever writes in it.

c.text:
Nothing comes out and nothing goes in. At {about|something like|roughly} {few} {in the morning|first thing|before noon} the turf settles, once, the way ground settles when weight comes off it rather than on.
By daylight the spade has been put away in the shed, and the shed was locked all night.

a1.text: The occupant has been dead for centuries and is {dressed for a journey|dressed for travelling}, and laid on their chest, new, wrapped in oilcloth, is the thing {somebody|someone} brought back to them.

a2.text:
{Turf, tamped, watered from the party's own bottles so it takes|Turf back, tamped down, and watered out of the party's own bottles so it takes}. The spade goes back against the wall.
At the gate {somebody|someone} has left a purse on the post, heavy, with nothing in it but coin, and no one is on the road in either direction.

b1.text: Three hundred years of a parish, and the {many} entries, and {a good deal|a great deal|rather a lot} that certain families would pay to have and rather more that they would pay to have burned.

b2.text: The vestry door opens at {two|three|half past one} and it is not the parson, and the pen is {already|by now} in its hand, and the party is standing between it and the book.

n0.text:
{A gable end and half a bell tower|A gable and half a bell tower} standing out of the water, and the bell still in it, and the water around the tower is clear where everything else here is peat-black.
{The bell rings sometimes.|The bell rings now and then.} There is nothing left to swing it.

choices.text: Swim or pole out to the tower.
Work along the drowned street beneath you.
Wait on the bank for the bell.

a.text:
Inside the tower the water is waist-deep and warm and the stair goes up out of it to a bell-loft with dry boards. {Somebody|Someone} has been sleeping up here: a bed of reed, a fire scar, fish bones, and {lots} years of tally marks.
The last mark is today's.

b.text:
Under {two metres|three metres|a fathom} of black water there is a street: doorways, sills, a cart, and every door standing open because they all opened outward when the water came.
{The houses have not been emptied.|Nobody emptied the houses.}

choices.text: Take what is loose in the street and stay out of the doors.

c.text:
It goes {at dusk|at last light|as the light goes}, {few} strokes, and every frog and bird in the swamp stops for it and starts again after.
Whatever it is calling does not come while there is anyone on the bank to see it. The party is left with a bearing, an hour, and their whole skin.

a1.text: It comes up out of the water {at dark|after dark|when the light goes}, and it has been down there since the flood, and it is glad of the company in a way that is worse than anger. It gives what it has been keeping and asks only that {somebody|someone} knows the name of the place.

a2.text:
The rope is rotten and the bell rings anyway, {once, enormously|once, and enormously}.
Everything in this swamp that has been waiting {lots} years to be told the hour comes at the tower at speed.

b1.text: {Pewter, lead, a chest of tools under a bench|Pewter, lead, and a tool chest under a bench} and a strongbox in the third house that the water has kept better than {any bank would|a bank would have}.

b2.text:
The cart is worth nothing and the harness brasses are worth something and the anchor stone on the corner is worth carrying, and the doors are all left {exactly|precisely} as open as they were.
On the way back to the bank the water goes warm around the party, all {at once|at the same time}, and lets them go.

n0.text:
{The temple is open, swept, and empty of people|The temple is open, swept, and has nobody in it} at an hour when it should not be. On the offering table there is a place laid for one more.
The bowl at that place has the party's number of grains in it, and {nobody|no one} counted them out for a party this size.

choices.text: Take the place that has been laid.
Leave an offering of your own and go.

a.text:
{The floor is cold and the sitting is long|The floor is cold and the sitting goes on} and about the third hour it stops being uncomfortable in a way that is not physical relief.
Something is going through the party's business item by item, without hurry, and putting most of it down again.

b.text:
Behind the screen is a room of shelves and on the shelves is everything that has been given here for {few} hundred years, labelled, dated, and dusted this week.
There is a shelf with the party's arrival date {already|by now} written on the card.

choices.text: Put something on the empty shelf.
Take something off a full one.

c.text:
{Salt, a coin, and the good bread|Salt, a coin, and bread out of the party's own pack}, laid out {properly|correctly}, and the bowl at the empty place is left where it stands.
The road out is clear and stays clear, and the party is not ill this season, and it is a long season.

a1.text: It takes a memory that {nobody|no one} misses, and leaves in its place a thing that has been on the temple's books, unclaimed, {since the year the walls went up|since the walls were new}.

a2.text: {It has not finished|It was not finished}, and standing up in the middle of it is a way of saying no that the temple has heard {exactly|precisely} once before.

b1.text:
{leader} leaves what they were carrying and the card is written up in a hand {nobody|no one} sees move.
What is on the shelf next to it, given three hundred years ago by {somebody|someone} who never came back for it, is handed over as though it had always been meant for this party.

b2.text: {It comes off the shelf easily, which is the trouble.|It lifts off the shelf far too easily, which is the trouble.} Everything else on the shelves is now {a witness|a witness to it}.

n0.text:
{The curtain wall is sound|The curtain wall is still sound} and the gate is barred from inside, and round the north side there is a postern with a new lock on an eight-hundred-year-old door.
{The key is on a nail beside it.|There is a key on a nail beside it.}

choices.text: Knock at the main gate and wait.

a.text:
Inside the bailey the grass is cut and the well is drawing and there is not a soul in the place. The hall is laid for {lots} and the fire is banked.
Everything is ready. It has been ready {for some time|for a while|a good while now}.

b.text:
The wall walk is clear and from up here the bailey shows what the ground does not: {the whole of|all of} it has been dug over and filled in, in strips, by {somebody|someone} working alone with a spade over a great many nights.
There is one strip left undug, against the chapel wall.

c.text:
It takes half an hour {and then|then|and after that} the wicket opens and a {very|remarkably} old servant of a family that has been gone from here for two centuries takes the party's names, thanks them, and closes it again.
On the step afterwards there is a purse of the old coinage, which is still gold, whoever's face is on it.

a1.text:
The food is real and hot and it is the best meal any of them has had in {a year|two years|a very long time}, and the fire draws, and afterwards everybody sleeps in beds and nothing at all happens.
{They wake up whole, and better than whole.|They wake whole, and better than whole.}

a2.text: The stair goes up {few} floors past {few} hundred years of a family's belongings, and the room at the top has one occupant, and it has been waiting for the postern key to be used.

b1.text: {Two feet|Three feet|A yard} down, wrapped in oiled canvas, is what the family took off the altar the night before the castle fell, buried by {somebody|someone} who came back for it and could not remember which strip.

b2.text:
He is in the gatehouse and he is {ninety|eighty-eight|ninety-one} and he has been digging up his own family's bailey for sixty years looking for one thing.
He does not want help. He wants {somebody|someone} to carry out the rest of what he has found, because he cannot lift it any more, and to take a fair share for the carrying.

n0.text:
One shop on a busy street has its shutters down {at noon|in the middle of the day|at midday}, and the people going past it go round a piece of pavement in front of it without looking at what they are avoiding.
{The letterbox is full.|The letterbox will not take another thing.} The bell, when {leader} presses it, is answered instantly.

choices.text: Ask on the street about the shop.
Clear the letterbox and read the letters.

a.text: Behind the shutters it is a shop, stocked, lit, and the stock is not the sort that is sold from a street like this. {Nobody|No one} is behind the counter. There is a ledger open on it, {in credit|and it is in credit}, and a note asking whoever comes in to mind the place for an hour.

choices.text: Take from the stock and go.

b.text:
{Nobody|No one} on this street will say the shop's name, but four people, separately, say the same sentence about it, word for word, as though they had all been told what to answer.
